source: RFC 7693 (https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc7693.txt) Appendix A, B and E; BLAKE2 reference keyed KATs https://github.com/BLAKE2/BLAKE2/blob/ed1974ea83433eba7b2d95c5dcd9ac33cb847913/testvectors/blake2s-kat.txt and https://github.com/BLAKE2/BLAKE2/blob/ed1974ea83433eba7b2d95c5dcd9ac33cb847913/testvectors/blake2b-kat.txt (SHA-256: a915b96fc07f6ece3b3355a5cbb813dbf9cd0ad37c22a9b89bf11f9c47922418 / 82fcb3cabe8ff6e1452849e3b2a26a3631f1e2b51beb62ffb537892d2b3e364f)

filter: RFC: everything printed in Appendix A/B, transcribed and lower-cased; words (m, v, h) are as printed (big-endian hex of each little-endian word), v given as printed at i = 0 (after initialisation, before round 1) and after each round i (BLAKE2b 12 rounds, BLAKE2s 10). Appendix E: the two 32-byte grand hashes plus the parameter sets of the self-test (inputs and keys come from selftest_seq, a Fibonacci generator: a = 0xDEAD4BAD*seed, b = 1, out[i] = (a+b)>>24 per step). KAT: key 000102...(32 bytes for BLAKE2s, 64 for BLAKE2b), messages 00 01 02 ... of length 0..255; only messages of at most 128 bytes are kept; full-length digests (32 / 64 bytes).
